analysis.title: GS Materials Nov 17: mud and wall, Oversold signals, CESCO starts, Iron ore new lows, FM amber light, SBM initiation
key_insights: Iron ore hit fresh lows at $87. Onshore conference feedback was that CMRG (China's central iron ore buyer) has little appetite to block a second product from FMG. The author reads this as bullish FMG and bearish iron ore.
China was the majority seller in metals overnight. The author said the day before that China was selling everything.
CESCO headlines: Mercuria says concentrate supply growth is limited through 2028. Robert Friedland flagged the risk that the treasury charge (TC) benchmark system breaks.

Panama President Mulino gave his ministers the go-ahead to negotiate with First Quantum on a re-opening of its mine, citing arbitration risk if no deal is reached. The author notes the language moved from 'orderly shut' to 're-open'.
Zambia's state miner plans a $2.7B investment to boost mining and power output.

The question for metals is what reason there is to step in today. The author finds it hard to answer given the APEC summit, the trilateral meeting, CESCO and SHFE copper week, and Thanksgiving. The most bullish point in GS's China outlook is the base effect ('still bad, just less bad').
China's rare earth export ban was delayed until January, the second delay. The tariff threat remains. The author expects rare earths and copper to occupy at least two seats at the negotiating table.
Lithium Americas delayed the US-backed Thacker Pass project by 5 months (to 3/31/29 from 10/31/28). It may face a funding shortfall after a capex revision of +$900M.

Upcoming company events: BHP site trip next week, VALE CMD the week after, GLEN the week after that, RIO possibly. Boliden reports Dec 8 on Garpenberg. Antofagasta: market wants the Caserones update and Pelambres running versus guidance, which needs grades to improve in Q4.

Anglo American (AAL) is about the deal: Diamonds progressing, Nickel timeline Dec 21, Coal in 2027 (needs FIRB approval), Teck deal targeted for 1Q27. Glencore focus is DRC, Kazzinc and buybacks, which have been aggressive at current levels.
ArcelorMittal (MT.NA) is the market favourite as a recovery trade. Q4 consensus is 2.12bn and FY is 10.6bn. At 6x the stock is at today's price. Peers: NUE 7x, TATA 7x, TX 4x, SZG 4x.
The sector has been weak versus SXPP, and the year-end shape resembles 2018 (China trade war 1.0). Dec 2025 was when the 'debasement' move accelerated.

Oil: the desk has an appetite to sell, but wants the second derivative of energy prices to peak first. The author suggests China and CMRG could control supply as well as price, citing Indonesia's approach of leaving it in the ground when prices are unfavourable.

Precious metals: no appetite for downside. The market is restructuring into longer-dated upside trades (Cal27 is about as far out as liquid). GS 2027 outlook for precious metals is titled 'It Is 2022 Again'.
GS CTA view on rates: 26 of 27 modelled trend signals are negative, and GS forecasts the CTA community will net sell duration this week.

Copper: GS keeps its forecast of $15,400/t in 2027 (13% above spot) after the midterms, with two downside risks: AI-related positioning and US tariffs. Combined COMEX and LME net length fell to about 9% of open interest from about 21% at end-September.

Copper equities and price are trading as an AI trade. Managed money length is at 1-year lows. China premiums keep rising while SHFE on-warrant stocks sit at lows, so the physical signal is strong while price falls.

SBM Offshore initiated with Buy, TP EUR43 (25% upside). SBM holds about 40% FPSO market share, and the GS team expects a deepwater FID wave across Guyana, Brazil and West Africa that consensus does not reflect.

BP appointed Stuart Chambers and Andrew Bonfield as non-executive directors. The author reads Chambers as an indication the AAL/Teck deal goes through, since Teck gets the chair and head office and AAL gets the CEO and CFO.

China wrap: GS Optical Network -2.66%, GS Domestic AI +1.69%, Unitree -11.97%. A US restriction on China's remote AI compute access is seen as positive for domestic chips. CSI 300 and CSI 1000 ETFs picked up volume into the close.

tension_points.bull_case: GS keeps its $15,400/t 2027 forecast (13% above spot), with net length already down to about 9% of open interest from about 21% and the market starting to underwrite tariff risk given the asymmetry.
tension_points.bear_case: Two downside risks to the forecast: AI-related positioning and US tariffs. Copper is trading with AI baskets and China is the majority seller.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Tariffs remain the key risk, and a further unwind in AI-related positioning would hit copper.
